dialect: Modern Fortran (2008 to 2023 standards), free-form text, built with gfortran

size.label: different keywords in Fortran 2018
size.detail: Fortran has no reserved words. A keyword can also be a name, for example a variable called real.

size.label: built-in procedures (idioms)
size.detail: Functions and subroutines that come with the language, for example SQRT, SUM and MATMUL.

size.label: statement words (verbs and structure words)
size.detail: For example PRINT, ALLOCATE, IF, DO, MODULE and CONTAINS.

size.label: attributes (adjectives)
size.detail: For example ALLOCATABLE, PARAMETER and INTENT(IN).

words.meaning: A whole number, for example -1, 0 or 42.
A number with a decimal point, for example 3.14.
A value that is true or false.
Text.
A complex number: a real part and an imaginary part.
A new noun that you make from other nouns (a derived type).
Separates the description from the names in a declaration.
Put the value on the right into the name on the left. It is not the maths "equals".
The value never changes (a constant).
This name holds a list or a table of values (an array).
The program sets the size of this array when it runs.
This name points to a different value.
A pointer can point to this value.
Keep this value between calls.
Select the precision: how many digits a number keeps.
Make space for an ALLOCATABLE array.
Release the space of an array.
Add and subtract.
Multiply and divide. A division of two whole numbers drops the fraction: 7/2 is 3.
Raise to a power. x**2 is x times x.
Group a part of a formula, as in maths.
Square root.
The size of a number without its sign.
Sine and cosine. The angle is in radians.
The angle of a point (y, x).
The exponential and the natural logarithm.
The remainder after a division.
The largest / smallest of the values.
Round to the nearest whole number.
Round down to a whole number.
Change a whole number into a REAL.
Change a REAL into a whole number. It drops the fraction.
Do a block only if a condition is true.
Starts the block to do when the condition is false.
Choose one block from many, by the value of one name.
Do a block again, a number of times.
Do a block again while a condition is true.
Stop the loop now.
Go to the next turn of the loop.
Stop the program.
Compare two values: equal, not equal, less, greater, less or equal, greater or equal.
Join or reverse conditions.
All the values of the array x.
The values of x from position 2 to position 5.
Change only the values that meet a condition.
In DO CONCURRENT: the steps can happen in any order, so the compiler can do them at the same time.
Add all the values.
Multiply all the values.
The largest / smallest value.
The position of the largest value.
How many values meet a condition.
True if one value / all values meet a condition.
How many values an array holds.
Multiply two lists value by value, then add the results.
Multiply two matrices (tables of numbers).
Turn the rows of a table into columns.
Give the same values a different shape.
The start of the primary program.
The end of a program, module, subroutine or function.
A named box of related names and procedures.
Make the names in a module available here.
The procedures come after this line.
A named procedure that does a job.
A named procedure that returns one value.
Every name must have a declared type. Without it, old Fortran guesses the type from the first letter.
Run a subroutine.
This argument comes in, and the procedure must not change it.
The procedure gives this argument its value.
This procedure changes nothing outside itself.
Write the procedure for one value. Fortran then applies it to each value of an array.
Hide a name inside its module, or show it to other code.
Starts a comment. The compiler ignores the rest of the line.
The statement continues on the next line.
Show values on the screen.
Write values to the screen or to a file.
Read values from the keyboard or from a file.
Connect a file to a unit number.
Disconnect a file.
In PRINT and READ: let Fortran choose the layout.
A layout pattern. F8.2 is a number 8 characters wide with 2 decimals.
A built-in module with the words to talk to C code, and through C, to the hardware.
Make this procedure or type match the layout of the C language.
A built-in module with exact sizes, for example INT32 and REAL64.
Read the count of clock ticks.
Read the processor time that the program used.
Ask the operating system to run a command.
